A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FGG research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison: Appendices A–H in v2 and A–I in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original POP909 experiments, ablations, a 31-participant listening study, and appendix results for chord-only generation and guidance-weight sensitivity.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and reports additional evaluation metrics, comparison methods, and a condition-encoding ablation.

M1.justification: The FGG architecture, conditioning losses, sampling projections, and DDPM/DDIM procedures are retained. Negative values for chord-only conditioning already appear in v2 Figure 2 and Appendix B.1. The added inpainting architecture is a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions use POP909 for accompaniment and chord-only generation and describe Dorian and Chinese pentatonic generation examples. V3 Appendix E documents controls for these existing examples without establishing additional task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds an inpainting comparator and post-sampling rounding to the nearest in-key pitch. V2's note-deletion comparator is retained under a more explicit label. WholeSongGen and GETMusic membership in the corresponding benchmark comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The main evaluations replace pitch, duration, and note-density OA metrics with beat-level direct chord accuracy and chord/piano-roll IoU measured at 16th-note steps. This substantially changes the evaluation criteria in Tables 1–2. Dataset splits, training budgets, and listening-study design remain unchanged; the appendix guidance-weight study retains OA.

E4.justification: The central ablation study expands to test sampling guidance against inpainting and pitch rounding. A new footnote ablation tests whether negative values are needed to distinguish missing rhythmic conditioning. Earlier training/sampling ablations, guidance-weight sensitivity, and note-replacement examples are retained.

E5.justification: V3 removes Section 5.1.5's explicit statement that ablation experiments share random seeds. This reduces seed reporting without establishing that the seeds actually changed. The existing 95% confidence-interval reporting practice is retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remove OA entries and report new metrics, including FGG direct chord accuracy of 0.485 and chord/piano-roll IoU of 0.769/0.281. Table 2 adds inpainting and rounding results; the encoding ablation reports chord similarity falling from 0.767 to 0.705. Retained out-of-key and chord-similarity scores, listening results, and Tables 3–4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 revises the derivation following Equation 32, changing delta terms and replacing an inequality with equality. These are mathematical revisions beyond notation or explanatory rewriting. The stated propositions and convergence rates remain unchanged; the edits do not by themselves establish correctness.

C1.justification: The abstract withdraws the claim that the interactive demo is among the first in the symbolic-music literature. The central claims about precise guided generation, theoretical characterizations, and efficient interactive use remain.

C2.justification: New Section 6 specifies limitations from 16th-note quantization, required beat annotations, and unsupported abstract or probabilistic controls. V3 also discusses ambiguity in ground-truth agreement metrics and interprets the added inpainting comparator as imposing architectural and computational overhead. These extend v2's existing tonal and artistic limitations.

D1.justification: V3 announces a complete source-code release, supplies a repository address, and updates demo access information. New Appendix E gives pitch-class constraints, chord progressions, and timing instructions for existing mode-generation examples. The documented training hyperparameters, hardware, and generation time are retained.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to controllable RNN/GAN/VAE music systems and image inpainting, discussing Meade, Dong, Wu and Yang, Lugmayr, Xie, and Corneanu. It positions FGG in relation to guided completion and precise real-time control. Hsiao et al. (2021) is removed; publication-metadata updates are otherwise incidental.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the contribution summary and related-work narrative, condenses the statistical motivation, adds methodological subheadings, and reorganizes ablations into explicit variants. It introduces a limitations section and demo appendix and relocates the MOA explanation to the guidance-weight appendix.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting, substantially resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Tables 1–2 receive replacement metric columns, and Table 2 gains comparator rows. The six figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added alternative-method and encoding ablations strengthen evidence for FGG's design choices. Specific limitations, demo-generation instructions, and code-access information also improve the paper's usefulness. These are limited gains to an already substantial empirical study: main-table OA evidence and explicit shared-seed disclosure are lost, while the principal retained results and theorem statements remain unchanged.
